proposals.prompt:
Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Demonstration 1 (required items: apple, eggs, milk):
  0: {at(0,5)} E
  1: {at(1,5)} INTERACT
  2: {at(1,5)} E
  3: {at(2,5)} E
  4: {at(3,5)} N
  5: {at(3,4)} E
  6: {at(4,4)} E
  7: {at(5,4)} E
  8: {at(6,4)} INTERACT
  9: {at(6,4)} W
 10: {at(5,4)} INTERACT
 11: {at(5,4)} W

 17: {at(1,3)} W
 18: {at(0,3)} N
 19: {at(0,2)} N
 20: {at(0,1)} INTERACT

 22: {at(0,2)} S

 26: {at(1,5)} E
 27: {at(2,5)} E
 28: {at(3,5)} E
 29: {at(4,5)} E
 30: {at(5,5)} E
 31: {at(6,5)} E
 32: {at(7,5)} E
 33: {at(8,5)} E
 34: {at(9,5)} EXIT
 35: {at(9,5)} <terminal>

Propose norms using ONLY the atoms listed above. Do NOT define any new state properties or events: "abstraction" must be {}.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: Before leaving, shoppers are obliged to interact with the entrance station at cell (1,5).
Before leaving, shoppers are obliged to interact with the customer-service point at cell (0,1).
Before leaving, shoppers are obliged to interact with the station at cell (6,4).
After interacting at cell (6,4), shoppers are obliged to interact at the adjacent station at cell (5,4).
After interacting at cell (5,4), shoppers are obliged to interact with the weighing point at cell (2,4).
Shoppers are prohibited from moving north out of the bottom aisle except from cell (3,5).
Shoppers are prohibited from entering the restricted upper-central cells of the store.
Shoppers are prohibited from moving east from cell (6,4), requiring them to turn back west from that station.

s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: Anyone who takes a shopping cart is obliged to return it to the customer-service cart return before leaving.
It is forbidden to put a shopping cart down anywhere except the customer-service cart return.
It is forbidden to leave the supermarket while still pushing or holding a shopping cart.
Customers are forbidden to take shelf items unless they currently have a shopping cart.
Customers are forbidden to carry grocery items by hand rather than placing them in a cart.
At the beginning of a shopping trip, the customer is obliged to check out a cart from the entrance cart station.
After picking up any required item with a cart, the customer is obliged to return the cart to customer service before exiting.
Shopping carts are forbidden in the exit-side travel corridor, so customers must park the cart before walking to the exit.

Identify the hidden distinctions and use them to define higher-level state properties and/or events (in "abstraction"), possibly hierarchically, and propose norms expressed over them. Norms may also use the primitive atoms directly.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: Anyone who takes a shopping cart is obliged to return it to the customer-service cart return before leaving.
It is forbidden to put a shopping cart down anywhere except the customer-service cart return.
It is forbidden to leave the supermarket while still pushing or holding a shopping cart.
Customers are forbidden to take shelf items unless they currently have a shopping cart.
Customers are forbidden to carry grocery items by hand rather than placing them in a cart.
At the beginning of a shopping trip, the customer is obliged to check out a cart from the entrance cart station.
After picking up any required item with a cart, the customer is obliged to return the cart to customer service before exiting.
Shopping carts are forbidden in the exit-side travel corridor, so customers must park the cart before walking to the exit.
